title: Liberty’s Satou Sabally out for remainder of season with head injury
content:
New York Liberty forward Satou Sabally will miss the remainder of the season, including the playoffs, the team announced on Thursday.

Sabally, who played in just 13 games this season, has been sidelined since suffering her second concussion in just more than eight months on June 23, when she was hit in the head and face in a game against the Las Vegas Aces. She sustained the first concussion while playing for the Phoenix Mercury in Game 3 of the 2025 WNBA Finals.

The Liberty announced last month that Sabally was taking an indefinite leave of absence due to the head injury. At the time, coach Chris DeMarco said the decision came under the guidance of Liberty’s performance staff. Despite Sabally clearing concussion protocol, she was still struggling with lingering concussion-related symptoms. Sabally started five games this season, averaging 10.4 points and 2.8 assists.

The Liberty signed Sabally to a two-year, $1.67 million contract in the offseason. She is set to earn $855,750 next season.

In a corresponding move, the Liberty announced the signing of developmental player Anneli Maley to a standard player contract and signed guard/forward Madison Scott to a developmental contract.

Injuries have hampered the Liberty this season, forcing DeMarco to deploy 14 starting lineups. Sabrina Ionescu, Leonie Fiebich, Sabally, Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones were at one point expected to be the Liberty’s go-to starters. Still, they started only two games together due to injuries.

Four games remain on the Liberty’s regular-season schedule once the WNBA resumes after the FIBA World Cup. They are currently tied with the Washington Mystics and Dallas Wings for sixth place in league standings with a 24-16 record. The Liberty own the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Mystics, but the Wings own it over the Liberty.

The injury also leaves Sabally out of World Cup competition with her national team in Germany.
